{{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA AmeriCup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2017 FIBA AmeriCup|2017 Argentina / Colombia / Uruguay]]|}} }} '''Jameel Marcus Warney''' (born January 31, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Seoul SK Knights]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook Seawolves]], leading the team to its first ever appearance in the NCAA Tournament and graduating as the school's all-time leader in several career categories. After going undrafted, Warney became the first Stony Brook player to reach the NBA when he made his debut with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on March 11, 2018. Warney continued to play in the G League and was traded to the [[Westchester Knicks]] in 2019. Warney moved his career overseas and signed with the [[Seoul SK Knights]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL) before the 2019–20 season. He is the only player to be named the KBL's Foreign MVP four times. Warney led the Knights to a regular season title and KBL Finals championship in 2022. Jameel Warney is widely considered a [[Seoul SK Knights]] legend, having played numerous seasons with the team. He also holds the record for the most seasons played with a single team among top-tier foreign players in the KBL and has gained the respect of many basketball and [[Seoul SK Knights]] fans in South Korea. ==Early life== Jameel Warney was born in [[New Brunswick, New Jersey]] to Denise and James Warney. He grew up in [[Plainfield, New Jersey]]. Warney stood 5 foot 10 inches tall at age 11. After not finding success at baseball, football or wrestling, he was recruited to play [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] by a friend's mother, even though Warney did not have much basketball knowledge at the time; he recalled tackling an opposing player in order to defend a layup in his second game.{{Cite web|title=Stony Brook's Warney has come a long way|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/stony-brook-s-jameel-warney-can-t-forget-loss-to-albany-l52763|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160218004347/http://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/stony-brook-s-jameel-warney-has-come-a-long-way-1.11467453|url-status=live|archive-date=February 18, 2016|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Newsday|language=en}}{{Cite magazine|last=Gardner|first=David|title=Stony Brook's Jameel Warney could be the country's most valuable player|url=https://www.si.com/college/2016/02/17/stony-brook-senior-jameel-warney-could-be-countrys-most-valuable-player|access-date=2022-02-15|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=February 17, 2016 |language=en-us}} Recruited by head coach Dave Boff, Warney attended [[Roselle Catholic High School]]. With the guidance of Boff, Warney overcame a poor work ethic that resulted in low middle school grades in order to perform well academically at Roselle Catholic and remain eligible for the NCAA. By his senior year of high school, Boff described Warney as a "borderline honor roll student" who did not miss a single day of school after being a consistent [[Truancy|truant]] in middle school. As a sophomore, Warney averaged 20.0 points, 12.0 rebounds and 4.0 blocks per game and was named All-Union County. During his junior year, Warney faced [[The Patrick School|St. Patrick's Catholic]] player [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]], a future [[2012 NBA draft|second-overall]] draft pick from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], in the playoffs and put up 20 points and 11 rebounds. He averaged 17.5 points, 13.4 rebounds and 3.4 blocks per game as a junior.{{Cite web|title=Men's hoops signs three to NLIs for 2012-13|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2011/11/9/Men_s_hoops_signs_three_to_NLIs_for_2012_13.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=November 9, 2011 |language=en}} In his senior season, he averaged 17.0 points, 13.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 3.5 blocks per game. He graduated as Roselle Catholic's all-time leading scorer.{{cite web |first=David |last=Gardner |url=http://www.campusrush.com/stony-brook-seawolves-jameel-warney-player-year-1607631209.html |title=Hungry Wolf: Jameel Warney May Be College Hoops' Mvp, But First He Wants To Make School History |work=CampusRush.com |date=February 17, 2016 |access-date=October 8, 2016}} Warney was originally expected to accept a scholarship to play college basketball at nearby [[Rider Broncs men's basketball|Rider]], but Stony Brook head coach [[Steve Pikiell]] and his assistant [[Jay Young (basketball)|Jay Young]] continued to heavily pursue him through a connection with Stony Brook player Bryan Dougher, who had played on the same AAU team before Warney.{{efn|Dougher became Stony Brook's leading scorer with 1,609 career points, a record which Warney would break in 2015.}} Before his senior year of high school, [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] expressed interest in Warney after he outplayed a prospect that Iowa was targeting. Once Iowa's interest was publicized, Warney earned attention from roughly 25 schools, including [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] and [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. However, Warney wanted to play immediately instead of redshirting or being a bench player at a power conference school, and he was drawn to Stony Brook during his official visit. "I loved the campus and the community. I thought it was beautiful," he said. Ranked as the number five recruit in New Jersey by EKB Scouting and the 49th-best power forward in the country by [[ESPN]], Warney officially committed to Stony Brook on August 12, 2011.{{Cite web|title=Jameel Warney Commits To Stony Brook - RealGM Wiretap|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/215149/Jameel-Warney-Commits-To-Stony-Brook|access-date=2022-02-15|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ==College career== === Freshman season === Warney made his collegiate debut in Stony Brook's season opener on November 9, 2012, against [[2012–13 Marist Red Foxes men's basketball team|Marist]], recording eight points and five rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Brenton, Coley lift men's hoops to 60-57 win at Marist|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2012/11/10/Brenton_Coley_lift_men_s_hoops_to_60_57_win_at_Marist.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=November 10, 2012 |language=en}} In his second game against [[Mount Ida College|Mount Ida]], Warney scored 16 points on a perfect 8-for-8 from the floor, becoming the first Stony Brook player in program history to attempt at least eight shots and make them all. He earned America East Rookie of the Week honors for these performances, the first Stony Brook player to be named since 2009.{{Cite web|title=Warney named America East Rookie of the Week|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2012/11/12/Warney_named_America_East_Rookie_of_the_Week.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=November 12, 2012 |language=en}} Playing against [[2012–13 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], Warney grabbed a then-best 11 rebounds. After the game, Huskies head coach [[Jim Calhoun]] visited the Stony Brook locker room to personally praise the 18-year old Warney.{{Cite web|last=Kussoy|first=Howie|date=2015-12-25|title=Stony Brook's 1-man wrecking crew lands on NBA radar|url=https://nypost.com/2015/12/25/stony-brooks-one-man-wrecking-crew-lands-on-nba-radar/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=New York Post|language=en-US}} Warney led Stony Brook with 17 points in a 76–69 loss to [[2012–13 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]].{{Cite web|last=Barker|first=Jeff|title=Terps hold off late rally for win over Stony Brook|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2012/12/21/terps-hold-off-late-rally-for-win-over-stony-brook/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=baltimoresun.com|date=December 21, 2012 }} He won eight America East Rookie of the Week awards en route to being named America East Rookie of the Year, second-team All-America East, America East All-Defensive Team and America East All-Rookie Team. He was the first Stony Brook player to win Rookie of the Year and the first Stony Brook freshman to be named to an All-America East team and the All-Defensive Team.{{Cite web|title=Men's hoops sweeps America East awards|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2013/3/8/Men_s_hoops_sweeps_America_East_awards.aspx?path=mbball|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics| date=March 8, 2013 |language=en}} Stony Brook was eliminated in the semifinals of the [[2013 America East men's basketball tournament|America East tournament]] to [[2012–13 Albany Great Danes men's basketball team|Albany]], losing 61–59 on a last-second layup.{{Cite web|date=2015-03-25|title=Black's game-winner lifts Albany over Stony Brook 61-59 to head to America East finals|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/blacks-game-winner-lifts-albany-over-stony-brook-61-59-to-head-to-america-east-finals|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Associated Press|language=en-US}} In the opening round of the [[2013 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], Warney had 16 as Stony Brook beat [[2012–13 UMass Minutemen basketball team|UMass]] 71–58 for the program's first-ever NIT win.{{Cite web|last=Plumer|first=Harry|date=2013-03-21|title=UMass ends season with 71-58 loss to Stony Brook in NIT first round|url=https://www.masslive.com/umassbasketball/2013/03/umass_ends_season_with_71-58_l.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=masslive|language=en}} Against [[2012–13 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] in the second round, Warney led Stony Brook with 17 points and seven rebounds, but the Seawolves lost 75–63 and ended the season with a 25–8 record.{{Cite web|last=Batterson|first=Steve|title=Marble leads Iowa to NIT win over Stony Brook|url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/iowa/marble-leads-iowa-to-nit-win-over-stony-brook/article_a477172e-936d-11e2-8046-001a4bcf887a.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Waterloo Cedar Falls Courier|date=March 22, 2013 |language=en}} Warney ended his freshman season averaging 12.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game. His .618 shooting percentage was the best in the America East, while he was the sixth-best in rebounds and second-best in blocks. He shot .650 in conference play. His 408 points were the most by any Stony Brook freshman along with his 165 field goals made.{{Cite web|title=Stony Brook Division I Record Book|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/stonybrook.sidearmsports.com/documents/2018/5/1/Division_I_Record_Book.pdf}} === Sophomore season === Warney won his first America East Player of the Year award during the [[2013–14 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|2013–14 season]], averaging 14.5 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game while shooting .616. He was also named first-team All-America East.{{Cite web|title=Warney named America East Player of the Year to headline five #Seawolves honorees|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/3/7/Warney_named_America_East_Player_of_the_Year_to_headline_five_Seawolves_honorees.aspx?path=mbball|access-date=2019-01-09|website=Stony Brook University Athletics| date=March 7, 2014 |language=en}} He was also named an [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention All-American, a [[Lou Henson Award|Lou Henson Mid-Major All-American]] and first-team All-Met.{{Cite web|last=Galotti|first=Joe|date=2014-03-31|title=Warney receives AP All-American honorable mention|url=https://www.sbstatesman.com/2014/03/31/warney-receives-ap-all-american-honorable-mention/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=The Statesman|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|title=Warney named Mid-Major All-American|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/3/28/Warney_named_Mid_Major_All_American.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=March 28, 2014 |language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Warney takes home All-Met first-team honors|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/4/22/Warney_takes_home_All_Met_first_team_honors.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=April 22, 2014 |language=en}} Warney became the first Stony Brook player to record three straight double-doubles. He set new career highs with a 23-point, 19-rebound double-double against [[2013–14 Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball team|Florida Atlantic]] and immediately bested those numbers with a 32-point, 21-rebound double-double against [[2013–14 Detroit Titans men's basketball team|Detroit]] in a 104–102 3OT win; Warney's 21 rebounds set a new program record at the time, and he shot 13-for-14.{{Cite web|title=Record performance, buzzer-beater lead #Seawolves to triple overtime win over Detroit|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2013/11/24/Record_performance_buzzer_beater_lead_Seawolves_to_triple_overtime_win_over_Detroit.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=November 24, 2013 |language=en}} He scored 12 points in the [[2014 America East men's basketball tournament|2014 America East championship game]] as Stony Brook lost 69–60.{{Cite web|title=#Seawolves come up short in NCAA Tournament bid|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/3/15/_Seawolves_come_up_short_in_NCAA_Tournament_bid.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=March 15, 2014 |language=en}} In the [[2014 College Basketball Invitational|CBI]] opening round against [[2013–14 Siena Saints men's basketball team|Siena]], Warney had 15 points and 10 rebounds, his tenth double-double of the season, and a new career-high five blocks.{{Cite web|title=#Seawolves 23-win season concludes with CBI loss at Siena|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/3/18/_Seawolves_23_win_season_concludes_with_CBI_loss_at_Siena.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=March 18, 2014 |language=en}} === Junior season === Warney repeated as America East Player of the Year for the [[2014–15 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|2014–15 season]], averaging 16.7 points, 11.7 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game, leading the conference in all of those statistics. He also won his first America East Defensive Player of the Year award and earned another first-team All-America East and All-Defensive Team selection.{{Cite web|title=Warney wins America East Player of the Year|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2015/3/2/Warney_wins_America_East_Player_of_the_Year.aspx?path=mbball|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics| date=March 2, 2015 |language=en}} He led all of Division I with 24 double-doubles and 409 rebounds, and was one of 17 players to average a double-double on the season. He tied former [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel]] star [[Malik Rose]]'s America East record for most rebounds in a season.{{Cite web|title=Warney named first team All-Met|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2015/4/22/Warney_named_first_team_All_Met|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=April 22, 2015 |language=en}} He had the most total rebounds in Division I and finished third in rebounds per game.{{Cite web|title=2014-15 Leaders|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/seasons/2015-leaders.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|language=en}} Warney scored his 1,000th career point against [[2014–15 LIU Brooklyn Blackbirds men's basketball team|LIU Brooklyn]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] in the NIT Tip-Off.{{Cite web|date=2015-03-24|title=Warney scores 1,000th career point, leads Stony Brook past LIU Brooklyn 73-54 in NIT Tip-Off|url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/warney-scores-1000th-career-point-leads-stony-brook-past-liu-brooklyn-73-54-in-nit-tip-off|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Associated Press|language=en-US}} He had an 18-point, 11-rebound, 8-block performance versus [[2014–15 Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball team|Loyola Maryland]].{{Cite web|title=Warney's big afternoon leads Stony Brook over Loyola Maryland, 67-52|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2014/12/21/Warney_s_big_afternoon_leads_Stony_Brook_over_Loyola_Maryland_67_52.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=December 21, 2014 |language=en}} In Stony Brook's first program win against a ranked opponent, No. 13 [[2014–15 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], Warney scored the go-ahead bucket.{{Cite web|title=Stony Brook stuns Washington with late run, beats Huskies 62-57|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/stony-brook-stuns-washington-with-late-run-beats-huskies-62-57/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=CBSSports.com|date=December 28, 2014 |language=en}} He set a conference record by winning eight straight America East Player of the Week awards. Despite a Warney double-double, Stony Brook lost in the [[2015 America East men's basketball tournament|America East championship game]] to [[2014–15 Albany Great Danes men's basketball team|Albany]] again, this time on a last-second [[Peter Hooley]] three. In the [[2015 College Basketball Invitational|CBI]] against [[2014–15 Mercer Bears men's basketball team|Mercer]], Warney's double-double was again not enough to overcome a last-second shot.{{Cite web|last=Vertsberger|first=David|date=2015-03-20|title=Nwamu's last-second shot ends Seawolves season in first round of CBI|url=https://www.sbstatesman.com/2015/03/19/nwamus-last-second-shot-ends-seawolves-season-in-first-round-of-cbi/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=The Statesman|language=en-US}} He was named as a finalist for the Lou Henson Award, an [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention All-American, a NABC All-District Team selection and first-team All-Met. Warney's 11.7 rebounds per game and 409 rebounds remain the single-season Stony Brook program record. His 575 points are the most by a Seawolves player in his junior season and were the most in a single season before he broke his own record the following year. === Senior season === Warney won his third consecutive America East Player of the Year in the [[2015–16 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|2015–16 season]], joining [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]]'s [[Reggie Lewis]] and [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]]'s [[Taylor Coppenrath]] as the only players to do so. He also won America East Defensive Player of the Year and America East All-Defensive Team for the second straight season and was named first-team All America-East for the third straight season.{{Cite web|last=Communications|first=America East|title=Warney Named Player of Year for Third Time to Highlight #AEHoops MBB Awards presented by Under Armour|url=https://americaeast.com/news/2016/2/29/210759287.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=americaeast.com|language=en}} He shot .630 and averaged 19.8 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 3.0 blocks in 33 games, leading the America East in shooting percentage, points, rebounds and blocks. He recorded 21 double-doubles in 33 games.{{Cite web|title=Warney named America East player of year|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/jameel-warney-named-america-east-player-of-year-for-3rd-time-1.11523719|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306165237/http://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/jameel-warney-named-america-east-player-of-year-for-3rd-time-1.11523719|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2016|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Newsday|language=en}}{{cite web|last=Karalla|first=Bobby|date=July 27, 2016|title=Mavs sign Jameel Warney and Keith Hornsby|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-jameel-warney-keith-hornsby/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818211019/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-jameel-warney-keith-hornsby/|archive-date=August 18, 2016|access-date=August 10, 2016|work=Mavs.com}} His 94 blocks were the fourth-most in Division I.{{Cite web|title=2015-16 Leaders|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/seasons/2016-leaders.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|language=en}} He led Stony Brook with 22 points and 11 rebounds against No. 17 [[2015–16 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] in a 79–72 OT loss.{{Cite web|last=Sparks|first=Adam|title=Vanderbilt men rally, beat Stony Brook in OT|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2015/11/19/vanderbilt-men-rally-beat-stony-brook-ot/76002872/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=The Tennessean|language=en-US}} Facing [[2015–16 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], Warney recorded both his 1,000th career rebound and 200th career block. With 29 points against [[2015–16 Northeastern Huskies men's basketball team|Northeastern]], Warney overtook Bryan Dougher (1,609) to become the top scorer in Stony Brook's Division I history.{{Cite web|date=2015-12-14|title=SBU's Warney Shatters Program's D-1 Scoring Record in Loss to Northeastern|url=http://sbpress.com/2015/12/stonys-warney-shatters-programs-d-1-scoring-record-in-loss-to-northeastern/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=The Stony Brook Press|language=en-US}} He set a new Stony Brook program record with nine blocks against [[2015–16 Princeton Tigers men's basketball team|Princeton]], adding 26 points, 15 rebounds and five assists as well.{{Cite web|title=The Statesman 12-7-2015 by The Statesman - Issuu|url=https://issuu.com/sbstatesman/docs/the_statesman_final_12-7|access-date=2022-02-15|website=issuu.com|date=December 6, 2015 |language=en}} On January 25, 2016, Warney passed [[Tommy Brenton]] (1,115) for the most career rebounds in Stony Brook history.{{Cite web|title=Rested Stony Brook crushes Maine|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/puriefoy-s-23-points-help-stony-brook-crush-maine-81-54-1.11392065|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129074553/http://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/puriefoy-s-23-points-help-stony-brook-crush-maine-81-54-1.11392065|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 29, 2016|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Newsday|language=en}} On February 8 versus [[2015–16 Hartford Hawks men's basketball team|Hartford]], Warney set a new career high with 36 points on 16-for-18 shooting, tying the Stony Brook single-game point record.{{Cite web|last=Gilbert|first=Skyler|date=2016-02-09|title=Warney's career-high keys Seawolves win against Hartford|url=https://www.sbstatesman.com/2016/02/09/warneys-career-high-keys-seawolves-win-against-hartford/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=The Statesman|language=en-US}} He won his 16th America East Player of the Week award, a new conference career record, on February 15.{{Cite web|title=Warney earns America East Player of the Week honors|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2016/2/15/Warney_earns_America_East_Player_of_the_Week_honors.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=February 15, 2016 |language=en}} Warney led Stony Brook to a nation-leading 18-game win streak and a 22–4 record. In a loss to [[2015–16 Albany Great Danes men's basketball team|Albany]], Warney surpassed Emeka Smith (1,978), a Division III player from 1989 to 1993, to become Stony Brook's all-time leading scorer.{{Cite web|date=2016-02-18|title=Local Roundup: UAlbany men halt Stony Brook streak|url=https://www.troyrecord.com/sports/local-roundup-ualbany-men-halt-stony-brook-streak/article_ed1d32b1-cf60-5c64-bc27-21f5de44823c.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=troyrecord|language=en-US}} He was named to the 35-man midseason watch list for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] and one of the final five finalists for the [[Karl Malone Award]], given to the best power forward in the NCAA.{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|date=February 11, 2016|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|work=[[Fox Sports]]|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016}}{{Cite web|title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Final Five Candidates Announced for 2016 Karl Malone Award|url=https://www.hoophall.com/news/final-five-candidates-announced-for-2016-karl-malone-award/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.hoophall.com|language=en}}{{Efn|Iowa State's [[Georges Niang]] would win the award. The other finalists were Kansas' [[Perry Ellis]], North Carolina's [[Brice Johnson]] and Iowa's [[Jarrod Uthoff]].|name=b}} He broke 2,000 career points on February 21 against [[2015–16 Maine Black Bears men's basketball team|Maine]], becoming the 110th player in Division I history to record over 2,000 career points and 1,000 career rebounds. Stony Brook won the America East regular season title for the second time in Warney's career with a 14–2 conference record.{{Cite web|title=Warney scores 2,000th point as SBU clinches title|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/jameel-warney-goes-over-2-000-points-as-stony-brook-clinches-title-1.11495116|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213101329/https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/jameel-warney-goes-over-2-000-points-as-stony-brook-clinches-title-1.11495116|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 13, 2019|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Newsday|language=en}} In the quarterfinals of the [[2016 America East men's basketball tournament|2016 America East tournament]], Warney scored 27 points and grabbed a career-high 23 rebounds in an 86–76 win over [[2015–16 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]]. His 23 rebounds broke the record for most rebounds in an America East tournament game.{{Cite web|title=Top-seeded Stony Brook advances past No. 8 UMBC, 86-76|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2016/3/2/top_seeded_stony_brook_advances_past_no_8_umbc_86_76.aspx|access-date=2020-03-24|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=March 2, 2016 |language=en}} He added another 21-point, 13-rebound double-double in the semifinals to advance Stony Brook to the championship game for the third season in a row.{{Cite web|title=Double-doubles from Warney, Puriefoy propel Seawolves into America East title game|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2016/3/7/Double_doubles_from_Warney_Puriefoy_propel_Seawolves_into_America_East_title_game.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=March 7, 2016 |language=en}} Down by 15 points in the second half to [[2015–16 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]], Warney scored 23 points on a perfect 11-for-11 shooting in the final 16 minutes of the game as Stony Brook came back to win 80–74, clinching the school's first NCAA Tournament bid in program history. Warney ended with both a career-high and single-game school record 43 points on 18-for-23 shooting; his 18 made field goals were also a new single-game school record.{{Cite web|last=Sherman|first=Rodger|date=2016-03-13|title=After heartbreak, Jameel Warney willed a win|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/3/13/11213894/stony-brook-jameel-warney-ncaa-tournament-america-east|access-date=2022-02-15|website=SBNation.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Kussoy|first=Howie|date=2016-03-12|title=Stony Brook claws out 1st NCAA berth behind Jameel Warney's 43|url=https://nypost.com/2016/03/12/stony-brook-claws-out-1st-ncaa-berth-behind-jameel-warneys-43/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=New York Post|language=en-US}} He was named America East tournament MVP for his heroics, averaging 30.3 points and 15.3 rebounds per game in the tournament.{{Cite web|last=Communications|first=America East|title=Warney's Record Performance Leads Stony Brook to First #AEHoops MBB Crown|url=https://americaeast.com/news/2016/3/12/210797228.aspx|access-date=2022-02-15|website=americaeast.com|language=en}} In the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]'s round of 64, Stony Brook was given a 13-seed and faced 4-seed [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. The Seawolves lost 85–57, but Warney dropped 23 points and 15 rebounds to end his collegiate career with 60 career double-doubles.{{Cite web|title=Stony Brook, Warney blown away by Kentucky in First Round|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2016-ncaa-tournament-march-madness/2016/3/17/11259542/2016-ncaa-tournament-recap-stony-brook-seawolves-kentucky-wildcats-warney|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.midmajormadness.com|date=March 17, 2016 |language=en}} His 19.8 points per game, 655 points and 3.0 blocks per game are single-season Stony Brook records. Warney graduated averaging 15.8 points, 9.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 2.0 blocks and 30.7 minutes per game in 135 games played, ending as the school's all-time leader in points (2,132), rebounds (1,275), blocks (275) and games played. He won 97 games in his Stony Brook career, the most by a single player in school history.[[File:Jameel Warney at Stony Brook University, Retired Number.jpg|thumb|200x200px|Warney's No. 20 was retired by Stony Brook in 2017.]] On February 18, 2017, Warney's No. 20 was retired by Stony Brook, becoming the first basketball player in school history to have his number retired.{{Cite web |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/stony-brook-retires-jameel-warney-s-no-20-jersey-1.13145546 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313090659/http://www.newsday.com/sports/college/stony-brook/stony-brook-retires-jameel-warney-s-no-20-jersey-1.13145546 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 13, 2017 |title=Stony Brook retires Warney's No. 20 jersey |website=Newsday |language=en |access-date=2019-04-04}} ==Professional career== ===Texas Legends (2016–2018)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Warney joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |first=Arya |last=Ahmadi |url=http://www.mavs.com/2016-mavericks-vegas-summer-league-roster/ |title=Samsung NBA Summer League 2016 Roster and Schedule |work=Mavs.com |date=July 4, 2016 |access-date=October 8, 2016}} On July 27, 2016, he signed with the Mavericks, but was later waived on October 16 after appearing in three preseason games.{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19790 |title=Mavericks waive Jameel Warney |work=InsideHoops.com |date=October 16, 2016 |access-date=October 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018184315/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19790 |archive-date=October 18, 2016 |url-status=dead}} On October 30, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Mavericks.{{cite web |url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/ |title=Legends Announce Training Camp Roster |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=October 30, 2016 |access-date=November 4, 2016}} In his first season with the Legends, he averaged 17.3 points per game.{{Cite web |url=https://www.sbstatesman.com/2017/10/15/jameel-warney-waived-by-mavericks-one-day-after-signing-deal/ |title=Jameel Warney waived by Mavericks one day after signing deal |last=Adams |first=Mike |date=2017-10-15 |website=The Statesman |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-21}} On October 13, 2017, he was signed by the Mavericks for the second time.{{cite web |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-jameel-warney-request-waivers-brandon-ashley/ |title=Mavericks sign Jameel Warney; request waivers on Brandon Ashley |work=Mavs.com |date=October 13, 2017 |access-date=October 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014083312/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-jameel-warney-request-waivers-brandon-ashley/ |archive-date=October 14, 2017 |url-status=dead}} He was later waived before the start of the season and rejoined the Legends. Warney played 42 games in the 2017–18 season and was named to the First Team [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League]] after averaging 19.9 points and 9.6 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/mvp-lorenzo-brown-headlines-2017-18-all-nba-g-league-first-team/ |title=MVP Lorenzo Brown Headlines 2017-18 All-NBA G League First Team |website=NBA G League |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-21}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2018)=== On March 7, 2018, the Mavericks signed him to a 10-day contract.{{cite web |title=Mavericks To Sign Jameel Warney To 10-Day Deal |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/249186/Mavericks-To-Sign-Jameel-Warney-To-10-Day-Deal |website=RealGM |access-date=March 8, 2018 |date=March 7, 2018}} Warney made his NBA debut on March 11, 2018, against the [[Houston Rockets]]. Warney played eight minutes and scored five points with four rebounds.{{Cite web |url=https://portjefferson.greaterlongisland.com/2018/03/12/jameel-warney-becomes-the-first-stony-brook-alum-to-reach-the-nba/ |title=Jameel Warney becomes first Stony Brook alum with NBA contract |date=2018-03-13 |website=GreaterPortJeff - greaterlongisland.com |language=en-US |access-date=2020-03-24 |archive-date=March 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324055824/https://portjefferson.greaterlongisland.com/2018/03/12/jameel-warney-becomes-the-first-stony-brook-alum-to-reach-the-nba/ |url-status=dead }} Warney made his return to New York on March 13 when the Mavericks faced the [[New York Knicks]]. Against the Knicks, Warney scored an NBA career-high eight points in 12 minutes.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975755 |title=Mavericks vs. Knicks - Game Recap - March 13, 2018 - ESPN |website=ESPN.com |language=en |access-date=2020-03-24}} === Anhui Dragons / Return to the Legends (2018–2019) === The Mavericks elected not to renew Warney's 10-day contract, returning him to the Legends.{{Cite web |url=https://www.mavsmoneyball.com/2018/3/21/17148618/dallas-mavericks-expected-to-sign-aaron-harrison-to-replace-jameel-warney-10-day-contract-g-league |title=Mavericks expected to sign Aaron Harrison to replace Jameel Warney |last=Crawford |first=Kate |date=2018-03-21 |website=Mavs Moneyball |language=en |access-date=2020-04-21}} On May 5, 2018, Warney signed with [[Anhui Dragons]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] to play during the summer.{{cite web |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/273266/dequan-jones-jameel-warney-sign-with-chinese-nbl-team-anhui.html#refresh_ce |title=DeQuan Jones, Jameel Warney sign with Chinese NBL team Anhui |work=Sportando.com |date=May 5, 2018 |access-date=May 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808233908/https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/273266/dequan-jones-jameel-warney-sign-with-chinese-nbl-team-anhui.html#refresh_ce |archive-date=August 8, 2018 |url-status=dead}} Warney tweaked his knee in July, prompting him to return home to recover.{{Cite web |url=https://lifestylefrisco.com/warney-back-for-year-three-with-legends/ |title=Warney Back for Year Three with Legends |date=2018-11-30 |website=lifestylefrisco.com |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-21}} ===Westchester Knicks (2019)=== On January 8, 2019, Warney was traded to the Westchester Knicks in exchange for [[Xavier Rathan-Mayes]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/jameel-warney-knicks-g-league-1.25702098 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110073759/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/jameel-warney-knicks-g-league-1.25702098 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 10, 2019 |title=Westchester Knicks trade for ex-SBU star Warney |website=Newsday |language=en |access-date=2019-01-09}} Warney scored 20 points and recorded 14 rebounds in a first round 95–82 playoff victory over the [[Windy City Bulls]], the Westchester Knicks' first playoff win in team history.{{Cite web |url=https://elitesportsny.com/2019/03/27/westchester-knicks-beat-windy-city-bulls-advance-in-g-league-playoffs-highlights/ |title=Westchester Knicks Claim First Ever Playoff Victory |last=Small |first=Danny |date=2019-03-27 |website=Elite Sports NY |language=en-US |access-date=2019-03-28}} ===Seoul SK Knights (2019–present)=== On July 17, 2019, Warney signed with the [[Seoul SK Knights]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].{{cite web |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola |title=Jameel Warney signs with SK Knights |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jameel-warney-signs-with-sk-knights/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 17, 2019 |date=July 17, 2019 |archive-date=July 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190717193428/https://sportando.basketball/en/jameel-warney-signs-with-sk-knights/ |url-status=dead }} In his first season with Seoul, Warney played 43 games in a shortened season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Warney led the Knights to a first-place 28–15 record while finishing fourth in the league in points per game (20.4) and third in rebounds per game (10.4).{{Cite web |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/jameel-warney-south-korea-coronavirus-1.43412478 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324055815/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/jameel-warney-south-korea-coronavirus-1.43412478 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 24, 2020 |title=Warney's season in South Korea is over because of pandemic |website=Newsday |language=en |access-date=2020-03-24}} Seoul was named co-champions due to the cancellation of the postseason.{{Cite web |url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2020/4/21/mens-basketball-jameel-warney-named-korean-basketball-league-foreign-mvp-member-of-leagues-best-five.aspx |title=Jameel Warney Named Korean Basketball League Foreign MVP, Member of League's Best Five |website=Stony Brook University Athletics |date=April 21, 2020 |language=en |access-date=2020-04-21}} Warney won the KBL's Foreign MVP award and was also named to the All–KBL Team.{{Cite web |url=https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200420006100315 |title=Son of legend wins 1st MVP award in men's basketball |last=유지호 |date=2020-04-20 |website=Yonhap News Agency |language=en |access-date=2020-04-21}} He re-signed with the team on September 26, 2020.{{cite web |title=SK Knights keep Warney for another season |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/South-Korea/news/646044/SK-Knights-keep-Warney-for-another-season |website=Asia Basket |access-date=September 26, 2020 |date=September 26, 2020}} In the 2020–21 season, Warney averaged 17.7 points (fourth in the KBL) and 8.6 rebounds per game. However, Seoul finished a disappointing 24–30 in ninth place. Warney won his second KBL Foreign MVP in the 2021–22 season. He was the league's leading scorer (22.6 ppg) and second in rebounds (12.4 rpg).{{Cite web |title=South Korean KBL Stats - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/63/South-Korean-KBL/stats/2022/Averages/Qualified/All/points/All/desc |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=basketball.realgm.com}} Seoul won the regular season title with a 40–14 record. Sweeping [[Goyang Orion Orions]] 3–0 in the semifinals, Seoul beat [[Anyang KGC]] in the KBL Finals, winning the series 4–1.{{Cite web |date=2022-05-11 |title=SK Seoul Knights take home first Championship title in 5 years |url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/2022/05/11/sports/basketball/Korea-KBL/20220511155723436.html |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en}} Warney averaged 26.3 points and 10.0 rebounds per game in the KBL Finals.{{Cite web |title=KBL 공식 홈페이지 |url=https://www.kbl.or.kr/game/archive-player |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=www.kbl.or.kr}} Warney won the third KBL Foreign MVP in four years for the 2022–23 season. He led the KBL in scoring again with 24.1 points per game and was third with 11.3 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |title=2023 Korean Basketball League Playoffs & Regular Season Awards Determined {{!}} EASL |url=https://www.easl.basketball/news/2023-korean-basketball-league-playoffs-regular-season-awards-determined |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=www.easl.basketball |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-11-01 |title=Interview: Samsung Thunders' new guy on the block is here to win |url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2023-11-01/sports/basketball/Interview-Samsung-Thunders-new-guy-on-the-block-is-here-to-win/1902758 |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en}} Seoul finished second in the regular season with a 36–18 record. The Knights swept the [[LG Sakers]] 3–0 in the semifinals. In a KBL Finals rematch with Anyang KGC, the series went to seven games, where Anyang won Game 7 in overtime, 100–97.{{Cite web |title=How Anyang KGC overcame great rival Seoul SK Knights to land the 2023 KBL championship {{!}} EASL |url=https://www.easl.basketball/news/how-anyang-kgc-overcame-great-rival-seoul-sk-knights-to-land-the-2023-kbl-championship |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=www.easl.basketball |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-05-08 |title=Anyang KGC beat Seoul SK Knights to win KBL championship |url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/2023/05/08/sports/basketball/Anyang-KGC-Seoul-SK-Knights-KBL/20230508165100678.html |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en}} In the 2024–25 season, Warney won his fourth MVP award, becoming the first player in KBL history to win four MVP awards, overtaking Johnny McDowell and [[Ricardo Ratliffe]]. He was the second unanimous winner in league history, besides McDowell in 1998.{{Cite web |last=CHOSUNBIZ |date=2025-04-09 |title=Warney confirms retirement plans and celebrates historic MVP victory in Korea |url=https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-sports/2025/04/10/QTJ7GV36SBHLXDOLOUZ4XJHAGQ/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=CHOSUNBIZ |language=en}} After the Knights won the regular season championship, Warney also announced that he intended to retire after the season. ==National team career== Warney played with the senior [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]], where he won a gold medal. He was named to the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]], and was also named [[FIBA AmeriCup Most Valuable Player|the tournament's MVP]]. He was named [[USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year]] for 2017.{{cite news |title=Jameel Warney Honored as 2017 USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year |date=December 15, 2017 |work=USA Basketball |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2017/12/male-athlete-of-the-year.aspx
